recipes.name: Som Tam Thai (Green Papaya Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crunchy shredded green papaya pounded with lime, palm sugar and fish sauce, sour and sweet first with a chili bite and toasted peanuts in every mouthful.
recipes.healthBenefit: Raw green papaya, beans and tomatoes bring vitamin C and fibre with very little fat, while the sauce carries a fair amount of salt and some sugar.

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a clay mortar to a rough paste, about 20 to 30 seconds.
Add the long beans and bruise them lightly with the pestle, then add the tomatoes and press just until they split.
Add the palm sugar, fish sauce and lime juice and stir with a spoon until the sugar dissolves, 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Add the shredded papaya, dried shrimp and peanuts, then pound gently while turning everything with the spoon for 30 to 60 seconds so the papaya softens a little and takes the dressing.
Taste for sour, sweet and salty, adjust with lime, sugar or fish sauce, and serve at once with sticky rice and raw cabbage.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the raw papaya, tomatoes and lime juice.
From the papaya and long beans.
Mostly from the fish sauce and dried shrimp.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Som Tum Thai (Green Papaya Salad)
Wikipedia, Green papaya salad

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai (single serve: 1 garlic, 1 chili, 1/4 cup beans, 5 tomatoes, 1 cup papaya, 2 tbsp each lime and palm sugar, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp dried shrimp, 2 tbsp peanuts) doubled, compared with Wikipedia on the Central Thai version being sweeter and carrying peanuts and dried shrimp.

recipes.name: Som Tam Lao (Isan Papaya Salad with Pla Ra)
recipes.flavorProfile: A fiercer, funkier papaya salad, deeply savoury from fermented fish and salted crab, hot with chilies and sour with lime, with almost no sweetness.
recipes.healthBenefit: Raw papaya, tomatoes and beans bring vitamin C and fibre, while the fermented fish, salted crab and fish sauce make it a salty dish best eaten with plenty of fresh vegetables.

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies in a clay mortar until broken down, about 20 to 30 seconds.
Add the long beans, eggplant and salted crab and bruise them, then add the tomatoes and press until they release their juice.
Add the palm sugar, fish sauce, pla ra juice and lime juice and stir until the sugar dissolves, about 1 minute.
Add the papaya and pound gently while turning with a spoon for 30 to 60 seconds, until it is well coated and slightly softened.
Taste, adding more pla ra for funk or lime for sourness, and serve at once with sticky rice, raw cabbage and long beans.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the raw papaya, tomatoes and lime.
From the papaya, beans and eggplant.
High, from the pla ra, salted crab and fish sauce.

citations.source: Import Food, Som Tum (Somtum Lao sai pla ra)
Wikipedia, Green papaya salad

recipes.curationNote: Import Food 1298 (4 servings: 2 cups papaya, 3 Roma tomatoes, string beans, 5 chiles, 3 garlic, 2 tbsp each palm sugar, fish sauce, lime and pla ra juice) followed, with the salted crab and eggplant Wikipedia names for the Lao and Isan version. Dried shrimp and peanuts left out since this style does not carry them.

recipes.name: Larb Moo (Isan Minced Pork Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Warm, juicy minced pork dressed with lime and fish sauce, nutty from toasted rice powder, hot from chili flakes and bright with handfuls of mint and shallot.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork gives a good amount of protein, B vitamins and zinc, and the herbs add freshness with little fat beyond what the meat carries.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Put the pork and water in a small pot over medium heat and cook, stirring to break it up, until just cooked through with some juice left, 3 to 5 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and season with the fish sauce, lime juice and chili flakes.
Stir in the shallots and toasted rice powder, then fold in the mint, cilantro, scallion and sawtooth coriander.
Taste for a balance of sour, salty and hot, then serve warm with sticky rice, cabbage wedges and long beans.

nutritionHighlights.note: Pork is one of the richest common sources.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Larb Gai (Ground Chicken Salad)
Wikipedia, Larb

Khao khua assumed 16 servings of 1 tbsp, prik pon the same.

recipes.name: Nam Tok Neua (Grilled Beef Waterfall Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky slices of grilled beef, still pink and juicy, tossed warm with lime, fish sauce, toasted rice powder, chili and a heap of fresh herbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef brings protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12, and the dressing adds flavour without added fat.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Grill the beef over hot charcoal or a grill pan at about 450°F (230°C) until charred outside and medium rare inside, 3 to 5 minutes a side.
Rest the beef for 5 to 10 minutes, then slice it thinly across the grain, keeping the juices.
Toss the warm beef and its juices with the fish sauce, lime juice and chili flakes.
Add the shallots and toasted rice powder, then the sawtooth coriander, cilantro, mint and scallion, and toss gently.
Serve at once with sticky rice and raw vegetables.

nutritionHighlights.note: Heme iron from the beef, absorbed well.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Neua Nam Tok (Beef Waterfall Salad)
Wikipedia, Larb
Wikipedia, Thai salads

recipes.name: Yum Woon Sen (Glass Noodle Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Slippery glass noodles and minced pork in a sharp lime and fish sauce dressing, with crunchy onion, celery, peanuts and the sweet tang of pickled garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork and peanuts add protein to a light noodle dish, while the noodles themselves are mostly starch with little else.

ingredients.baseName: Glass noodles made from mung bean starch

ingredients.cutPrep: sliced, plus 4 tbsp of its liquid

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

ingredients.cutPrep: Chinese celery, cut in 3 cm lengths

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil, cook the minced pork until no longer pink, 1 to 2 minutes, and lift it out.
In the same water cook the soaked glass noodles until clear and soft, 1 to 2 minutes, then drain and cut them a few times with scissors.
Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, pickled garlic liquid and chopped chilies until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the warm noodles and pork with the dressing, then add the onion, tomatoes, pickled garlic, celery, scallion and cilantro.
Scatter with peanuts and serve at once, while the noodles are still warm.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the lime, tomatoes and chilies.

recipes.name: Yum Neua (Grilled Beef Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Charred sliced beef with cool cucumber, carrot and onion in a sweet, sour and salty lime dressing with a gentle chili heat.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef gives protein, iron and vitamin B12, and the raw vegetables add vitamin A, vitamin C and crunch.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Rub the beef with the sesame oil and grill over high heat, about 450°F (230°C), until medium rare, 2 to 4 minutes a side.
Rest the beef for 5 to 10 minutes, then slice it thinly across the grain.
Stir the palm sugar, lime juice, fish sauce and chopped chilies together until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the beef with the carrot, onion, tomatoes, cucumber, scallion and cilantro, pour over the dressing and toss again.
Serve at once with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Yum Nua (Thai Beef Salad)
Wikipedia, Thai salads

recipes.curationNote: Hungry in Thailand recipe for 2 followed at its amounts (9 oz beef, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp palm sugar, 2 tbsp lime, 1.5 tbsp fish sauce, vegetables as listed). Wikipedia names yam nuea yang as the grilled beef yam.

recipes.name: Yum Pla Duk Fu (Crispy Catfish with Green Mango)
recipes.flavorProfile: A golden, airy tangle of fried catfish flakes that shatters on the tongue, eaten with a sharp green mango salad full of chili, shallot and cashews.
recipes.healthBenefit: Catfish adds protein and the green mango brings vitamin C, while deep frying makes this a rich dish to share.

ingredients.name: catfish
ingredients.cutPrep: skin on fillet or whole, grilled or baked then flaked

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Grill or bake the catfish at 400°F (200°C) until cooked and slightly dry, 20 to 30 minutes, then pick off the flesh and pound or chop it into fine fluffy flakes.
Heat the oil in a wok to about 350°F (175°C), fry the cashews until golden, 1 to 2 minutes, and lift them out.
Scatter the fish flakes into the hot oil so they puff into a raft, fry until deep golden and crisp, 3 to 5 minutes, then flip briefly and drain on paper.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and sliced chilies together, then toss with the green mango, shallots and cashews.
Pile the mango salad beside the crispy catfish and serve straight away so the fish stays crisp.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the green mango and lime.
Mostly from the frying oil and cashews.

citations.source: Thai Table, Crispy Catfish Green Mango Salad
Wikipedia, Thai salads

Wikipedia describes the fried flaked catfish with green mango. Catfish is not in the food database, so it is listed by name.

recipes.name: Yum Mamuang (Green Mango Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, mouth-puckering green mango in a salty sweet lime dressing with chili, shallot, peanuts and the savoury chew of dried shrimp.
recipes.healthBenefit: Green mango brings vitamin C and fibre, with peanuts adding some protein and healthy fat.
instructions: Stir the palm sugar, fish sauce, lime juice and chili flakes together until the sugar dissolves.
Put the mango and shallots in a bowl, pour over the dressing and toss well.
Add the peanuts and dried shrimp, toss once more and serve at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the green mango and lime.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Thai Mango Salad (Yum Mamuang)
Wikipedia, Thai salads

recipes.curationNote: Hungry in Thailand recipe for 2 followed at its amounts (1 tbsp each palm sugar, fish sauce and lime, 2 tsp chili flakes, 7 oz green mango, 1/3 cup shallot, 2 tbsp each peanuts and dried shrimp). Wikipedia Thai salads used for context on yam style.

recipes.name: Yum Talay (Spicy Seafood Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender shrimp, squid and mussels barely cooked and tossed warm in a hot, sour lime dressing with onion, tomato and the crunch of Chinese celery.
recipes.healthBenefit: Seafood gives lean protein, iodine, selenium and vitamin B12, with almost no added fat.

ingredients.cutPrep: Chinese celery, cut in 3 cm lengths

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Mix the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, garlic and chopped chilies until the sugar dissolves.
Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the shrimp, squid and mussels in batches just until opaque, 30 seconds to 90 seconds, then drain.
Toss the warm seafood with the dressing, then add the tomato, onion and celery and toss again.
Taste, adjust with lime or fish sauce, and serve straight away.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the shrimp, squid and mussels.
Mussels and squid are rich in it.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Yum Talay (Thai Seafood Salad)
Wikipedia, Thai salads

recipes.name: Plaa Goong (Grilled Shrimp Salad with Lemongrass)
recipes.flavorProfile: Lightly charred shrimp tossed in a roasted chili jam and lime dressing, perfumed with lemongrass, makrut leaf and mint, sweet, smoky and hot all at once.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp gives lean protein and selenium, and the herbs and lettuce add freshness, with some sugar from the chili jam.

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Grill the shrimp over high heat until just pink, 2 to 3 minutes in all, turning once.
Stir the nam prik pao, palm sugar, fish sauce and lime juice together until smooth.
Toss the warm shrimp with the dressing, then add the shallot, lemongrass, makrut leaves, chilies, mint and cilantro.
Spoon onto a bed of lettuce and serve at once.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Pla Goong (Spicy Grilled Shrimp Salad)
Wikipedia, Thai salads

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai recipe followed (3/4 lb shrimp, 3 cups lettuce, 1/4 cup each mint, cilantro and shallot, 1/8 cup lemongrass, 4 makrut leaves; dressing 2 tbsp nam prik pao, 1 tbsp palm sugar, 2 tbsp each fish sauce and lime). Wikipedia confirms phla kung with lemongrass, mint and nam phrik phao. Nam prik pao assumed 16 servings of 1 tbsp.

recipes.name: Yum Som O (Pomelo Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Juicy pomelo segments and sweet shrimp in a creamy coconut and chili jam dressing, finished with toasted coconut, peanuts and crisp fried shallot and garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pomelo brings vitamin C and the shrimp adds protein, with the coconut and fried toppings making it a little richer than most yum.
instructions: Simmer the shrimp in a little water until pink, 1 to 2 minutes, then drain and halve them.
Toast the coconut in a dry pan over medium-low heat, stirring, until golden, 2 to 4 minutes.
Stir the coconut milk, nam prik pao, fish sauce, palm sugar and lime juice together until smooth.
Gently toss the pomelo and shrimp with the dressing, taking care not to crush the pomelo.
Top with the toasted coconut, peanuts, fried shallots, fried garlic and cilantro, and serve.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Yum Som-O (Pomelo Salad)
Wikipedia, Thai salads

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai recipe followed (3 cups pomelo, 6 shrimp, 2 tbsp coconut flakes, 2 tbsp peanuts, 1 tbsp each fried shallot and garlic; dressing 2 tbsp coconut milk, 1 tbsp nam prik pao, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp palm sugar, 2 tbsp lime). Wikipedia confirms yam som o with palm sugar and coconut milk. Kati read as 4 servings of 1/2 cup from the bases file, hom jiew and nam prik pao 16 of 1 tbsp.

recipes.name: Pad Thai (Stir-Fried Rice Noodles with Tamarind)
recipes.flavorProfile: Chewy, glossy rice noodles that are sweet, sour and salty at once from palm sugar, tamarind and fish sauce, with crisp bean sprouts, soft egg and crunchy peanuts.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken, egg and tofu give a good amount of protein and the sprouts and chives add some freshness, though the sauce makes it a fairly sweet and salty plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: half for the sauce, half for the noodles

ingredients.baseName: Tofu, firm, prepared with calcium sulfate and magnesium chloride (nigari)

ingredients.cutPrep: thin flat rice noodles (sen lek), soaked in room temperature water 30 to 60 minutes

instructions: Melt the palm sugar with the fish sauce, tamarind and half the water in a small pan over medium heat until smooth, 2 to 3 minutes, then set it aside.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium high heat and fry the chicken until cooked, 2 to 3 minutes, then add the shallot, garlic, tofu, dried shrimp and preserved radish and fry for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the drained noodles and the rest of the water and toss until they soften, 1 to 2 minutes, then pour in the sauce and keep tossing until the noodles absorb it, 2 to 3 minutes.
Push the noodles to one side, crack the egg into the space, scramble it until nearly set, about 1 minute, then fold it through.
Add the garlic chives and half the bean sprouts and toss for 30 seconds, then serve with the rest of the sprouts, lime wedges, peanuts and chili flakes on the side.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chicken, egg, tofu and dried shrimp.
From the rice noodles and palm sugar.
From the fish sauce, dried shrimp and preserved radish.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Authentic Chicken Pad Thai
Wikipedia, Pad thai

recipes.curationNote: Hungry in Thailand (serves 2: 1/2 cup palm sugar, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp tamarind, 1/4 cup water; 5 tbsp oil, 1 cup chicken, 1/4 cup shallot, 2 garlic, 1/4 cup tofu, 1 tbsp dried shrimp, 1/4 cup preserved radish, 5 oz dry noodles, 1 egg, 3 chive stalks, 1 cup sprouts) followed, compared with Wikipedia on tamarind as the base and the dried shrimp, tofu, radish and chives. recipes.name: Pad See Ew (Stir-Fried Wide Noodles with Soy Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, wide rice noodles charred at the edges in a very hot wok, sweet and smoky from dark soy, with tender chicken, egg and the slight bitterness of Chinese broccoli.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chinese broccoli brings vitamins C and K and the chicken and egg give protein, while the soy and oyster sauces make it a salty plate.

ingredients.baseName: Rice, non-glutinous rice products, fresh noodles, rice noodles
ingredients.cutPrep: fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai), separated

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.cutPrep: stems sliced on the bias, leaves cut in 5 cm pieces

instructions: Mix the dark soy, oyster sauce, thin soy, vinegar and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat, fry the garlic for 10 to 15 seconds, then add the chicken and fry until nearly cooked, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the Chinese broccoli stems and fry for 30 seconds, then the noodles and the sauce, and spread them out so they sear against the wok, tossing only every 20 to 30 seconds, 2 to 3 minutes in all.
Push the noodles aside, scramble the egg in the gap until just set, about 1 minute, then add the leaves and toss until they wilt, 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Finish with white pepper and serve with chili vinegar and sugar on the table.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the soy and oyster sauces.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Pad See Ew
Wikipedia, Pad see ew

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai (serves 2: 8 oz fresh wide noodles, 1/2 cup chicken, 2 garlic, 2 cups Chinese broccoli, 1 egg, 2 tbsp sweet dark soy, 2 tbsp oyster, 2 tsp thin soy, 2 tsp vinegar, 2 tsp sugar) followed, compared with Wikipedia on gai lan, egg, both soy sauces and the white pepper finish.

recipes.name: Rad Na (Wide Noodles in Thick Gravy)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky seared wide noodles under a silky, peppery gravy with tender marinated pork and crisp Chinese broccoli, mild and comforting until you add chili vinegar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and thiamine and the Chinese broccoli adds vitamins C and K, with the gravy carrying a fair amount of salt.

components.note: or water, as some cooks use

ingredients.cutPrep: tapioca starch: 1 tbsp for the marinade, 3 tbsp slurried in 100 ml water

ingredients.baseName: Rice, non-glutinous rice products, fresh noodles, rice noodles
ingredients.cutPrep: fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai), separated
stems sliced on the bias, leaves cut in 5 cm pieces

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Mix the pork with the egg, palm sugar, oyster sauce and 1 tbsp tapioca starch and leave it for 15 to 30 minutes.
Toss the noodles with the dark soy, then sear them in half the oil in a very hot wok, spreading them out and turning once, until charred in spots, 2 to 3 minutes. Divide them between plates.
Heat the rest of the oil, fry the garlic until golden, 20 to 30 seconds, add the pork and fry until it changes colour, 1 to 2 minutes, then add the Chinese broccoli stems.
Pour in the stock, soybean paste, thin soy and white pepper and bring to a boil, then add the leaves and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir in the starch slurry and simmer until the gravy turns glossy and thick, 1 to 2 minutes, then ladle it over the noodles and serve with chili vinegar.

Taste Asian Food, Rad Na

recipes.curationNote: Hungry in Thailand (serves 4: 300 g pork, 600 g noodles, 1 L water, 200 g Chinese broccoli, 1 tbsp soybean paste, 1.5 tbsp light soy, 1 tsp white pepper, 3 tbsp tapioca in 100 ml water) followed. recipes.name: Pad Kee Mao (Drunken Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: Wide rice noodles tossed fiercely hot with garlic, fresh chilies, green peppercorns and a fistful of peppery holy basil, salty and a little sweet.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken gives protein and the beans, carrot and baby corn add fibre and vitamins, while the sauces make it a salty, spicy plate.

ingredients.baseName: Rice, non-glutinous rice products, fresh noodles, rice noodles
ingredients.cutPrep: fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai), separated

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green
ingredients.cutPrep: bird's eye chilies, pounded with the garlic

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies to a rough paste and mix the dark soy, oyster sauce, thin soy, sugar and vinegar in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic and chili paste until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and fry until nearly cooked, 1 to 2 minutes, then add the baby corn, carrot, long beans, red chili and green peppercorns and fry for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss over high heat until the noodles are coated and lightly charred, 2 to 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat, fold in the holy basil until it just wilts, about 15 seconds, and serve at once.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the carrot and red chili.
From the soy and oyster sauces.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Drunken Noodles (Pad Kee Mao)
Wikipedia, Drunken noodles

recipes.name: Khao Soi Gai (Northern Curry Noodle Soup with Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: A rich, gently spiced coconut curry broth over soft egg noodles and fall-apart chicken, topped with a crisp nest of fried noodles, sharp pickled greens, shallot and lime.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken gives plenty of protein, but the coconut milk makes this a rich bowl high in saturated fat, best balanced with the pickles, shallots and lime served alongside.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.cutPrep: fresh, flat; 340 g boiled, 110 g deep-fried for the topping
cut in small wedges, to serve

instructions: Fry the curry paste in about a quarter of the coconut milk in a pot over medium heat, stirring, until the oil separates and it smells toasty, 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the drumsticks and turn them in the paste for 2 minutes, then pour in the rest of the coconut milk, the stock and the water.
Season with the palm sugar, thin soy, dark soy and fish sauce and simmer gently, partly covered, until the chicken is tender, 30 to 45 minutes.
While it simmers, deep fry the 110 g of noodles in hot oil at 350°F (175°C) until crisp and golden, 30 to 60 seconds, and boil the rest until just tender, 1 to 2 minutes.
Put the boiled noodles and a drumstick in each bowl, ladle over the broth, top with the crisp noodles and cilantro, and serve with shallots, pickled mustard greens and lime.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chicken and egg noodles.
From the dark chicken meat and the spices in the paste.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Khao Soi (Northern Thai Curry Noodles)
Import Food, Chiang Mai Curry Noodles (Khao Soi)

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai (serves 4: 4 drumsticks, 2.5 cups coconut milk, 2 cups chicken broth, 2 cups water, 1 tbsp palm sugar, 1 tbsp each thin and dark soy, 16 oz fresh egg noodles with 4 oz fried) followed, compared with Import Food on the Chiang Mai garnishes. Paste assumed 16 servings of 1 tbsp (4 used), coconut milk read as 4 servings of 1/2 cup and stock 8 servings of 1 cup from the bases file. Rachel adds a chili oil; it is left as an optional table condiment and not counted.

recipes.name: Kuay Teow Reua (Boat Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: A small, dark, intensely beefy bowl, spiced with star anise and cinnamon, thickened with a little blood, with soft rice noodles, tender beef, meatballs and fried garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef brings protein, iron and vitamin B12, and the long-simmered bones add some collagen, though the soy sauces make each bowl salty.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Rice, non-glutinous rice products, fresh noodles, rice noodles

ingredients.cutPrep: 8 cloves, chopped and fried golden in the oil

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green
ingredients.cutPrep: bird's eye chilies, for the chili vinegar

instructions: Put the shank, bones and water in a large pot, bring to a boil and skim, then add the light and dark soy, galangal, rock sugar, coriander roots, star anise, lemongrass, pandan, makrut leaves, cinnamon and peppercorns.
Simmer gently, uncovered, until the shank is tender, 2 to 2.5 hours, then lift out the shank and slice it, and strain the broth back into the pot.
Fry the garlic in the oil over medium heat until golden, 2 to 3 minutes, and set it aside for the topping.
Add the beef balls to the broth and simmer for 5 minutes, then stir in the blood and simmer for 2 minutes more, without boiling hard.

Blanch each portion of noodles and sprouts for 10 to 20 seconds and put them in small bowls, dip the flank slices in the simmering broth for 10 to 20 seconds, then top with sliced shank, beef balls and broth, and finish with fried garlic and chili vinegar.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the shank, flank and beef balls.
From the beef and the blood.
High, from the light and dark soy sauces.

citations.source: SBS Food, Boat Noodles (Kuay Tiew Rua)
Hungry in Thailand, Thai Boat Noodles

Cassia is given as ground cinnamon, its closest database match in form.

recipes.name: Kuay Teow Tom Yum (Tom Yum Noodle Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin rice noodles in a clear pork broth that the diner turns hot, sour, sweet and salty with lime, fish sauce, sugar and chili, crunchy with peanuts and fragrant with garlic oil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork gives protein and the sprouts and herbs add freshness, while the fish sauce, sugar and garlic oil make it a salty bowl with some sweetness.

ingredients.cutPrep: thin rice noodles (sen lek), soaked 20 to 30 minutes
chopped and fried golden in the oil

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Fry the garlic in the oil over medium heat until golden, 2 to 3 minutes, and keep the garlic and oil together.
Bring the stock to a simmer, add the pork in small pinches and cook, stirring, until it is cooked through, 2 to 3 minutes.
In each bowl put a share of the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chili flakes, peanuts and a spoon of garlic oil.
Blanch each portion of noodles and sprouts in boiling water until just soft, 30 to 60 seconds, drain and add them to the bowls.
Ladle over the hot broth and pork, toss so the seasonings dissolve, and top with cilantro and green onion.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the fish sauce and stock.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Tom Yum Noodle Soup
The Woks of Life, Tom Yum Noodle Soup (Kuay Teow Tom Yum)

recipes.curationNote: Hungry in Thailand (serves 4: 3 1/3 cups broth, 7 oz ground pork, 3 tbsp lime, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 9 oz noodles, 4 tbsp garlic oil, 6 tbsp peanuts) followed, compared with The Woks of Life on seasoning each bowl rather than the pot. Broth points at the chicken stock base, assumed 8 servings of 1 cup.

recipes.name: Khanom Jeen Nam Ya (Rice Vermicelli with Fish Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, slightly sour fermented rice noodles under a thick, earthy fish and coconut curry warmed with krachai, eaten with crunchy raw beans, sprouts, lemon basil and a boiled egg.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fish gives lean protein and the raw vegetables add fibre and vitamins, with the coconut milk bringing richness and some saturated fat.
instructions: Poach the fish in the water until it flakes, 5 to 7 minutes, lift it out and flake it, keeping the water.
Pound the flaked fish with the curry paste and krachai into a coarse paste, 1 to 2 minutes.
Bring the coconut milk and fish water to a simmer, stir in the fish paste and simmer, stirring, until thick, 8 to 10 minutes, then season with sugar and fish sauce.
Coil the noodles onto plates, ladle the curry over, and serve with the lemon basil, long beans, bean sprouts and boiled egg on the side.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the raw beans and sprouts.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Khanom Jeen Nam Ya
Eating Thai Food, Thai Fish Curry (Nam Ya)
Wikipedia, Khanom chin

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai (serves 4: 2 tbsp red curry paste, 2 tbsp krachai, 1 cup each coconut milk and water, 1 cup tilapia, 1 tsp each sugar and fish sauce, 10 oz noodles, lemon basil, beans, sprouts, 2 eggs) followed, compared with Eating Thai Food on the Southern version with Krabi-style vegetables. Wikipedia places khanom jeen across Thailand; region given as Southern for this fish curry style. Paste 16 x 1 tbsp and coconut milk 4 x 1/2 cup, from the bases file.

recipes.name: Kuay Teow Khua Kai (Wok-Fried Noodles with Chicken and Egg)
recipes.flavorProfile: Wide rice noodles fried dry and smoky until crisp at the edges, with tender chicken, a lacy set egg and green onion, served on cool lettuce with sriracha.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken and egg give a good amount of protein and the lettuce adds a little freshness, with the oyster and soy sauces carrying salt.

ingredients.baseName: Rice, non-glutinous rice products, fresh noodles, rice noodles
ingredients.cutPrep: fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai), separated

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat, fry the garlic until golden, 15 to 20 seconds, then add the chicken and fry until cooked, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the onion and fry for 1 minute, then the oyster sauce, seasoning sauce, dark soy, white pepper and sugar.
Add the noodles and spread them in a thin layer, letting them crisp against the wok for 1 to 2 minutes before turning them.
Push the noodles aside, pour in the egg and let it set halfway, about 30 seconds, then fold it through with the green onion.
Serve on a bed of lettuce with sriracha on the side.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the oyster sauce and seasoning sauce.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Kuay Teow Kua Gai
Wikipedia, Kuaitiao khua kai

recipes.curationNote: Hungry in Thailand (serves 2: 2 tbsp oil, 1 garlic, 7 oz chicken thigh, 3/4 cup onion, 2 tbsp oyster, 1 tbsp Golden Mountain, 1 tsp dark soy, 1/2 tsp white pepper, 1/2 tbsp sugar, 10 oz noodles, 1 egg, 2 green onions) followed, compared with Wikipedia on its Bangkok (Talat Noi) origin and service on lettuce.

recipes.name: Khanom Jeen Nam Ngiao (Northern Pork and Tomato Noodle Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: A tangy, savoury pork and tomato broth, deep red from dried chilies and earthy from fermented soybean, over rice noodles with pickled greens, sprouts and crisp pork rinds.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork gives protein and the tomatoes add vitamin C and lycopene, while the shrimp paste, fermented soybean and pickles make it a salty bowl.

ingredients.cutPrep: dried red chilies, soaked and drained

instructions: Pound or blend the dried chilies, shallots, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, shrimp paste, turmeric and coriander to a smooth paste, 3 to 5 minutes.
Bring the stock to a boil, add the ribs and simmer, skimming, until tender, 40 to 50 minutes.
Fry the paste in the oil in a pan over medium heat until fragrant and darker, 3 to 5 minutes, then add the minced pork and fermented soybean sauce and fry until the pork is cooked, 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir the pork mixture into the broth with the blood cake and simmer for 10 minutes, then add the tomatoes and simmer until they just soften, about 5 minutes, and season with fish sauce.
Put noodles in each bowl, ladle over the broth with ribs and tomatoes, and serve with bean sprouts, pickled mustard greens, pork rinds and chili flakes.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork ribs and minced pork.
From the shrimp paste, fermented soybean and pickles.

citations.source: SBS Food, Thai Pork Rib Noodle Soup (Nam Ngiaw)
Wikipedia, Nam ngiao

recipes.curationNote: SBS Food (serves 4: 600 g ribs, 2 L chicken stock, 250 g mince, 2 tbsp fermented soybean sauce, 4 tomatoes, 300 g noodles, 200 g each sprouts and pickled greens, pork rinds; paste of 8 dried chilies, 150 g shallot, 4 garlic, galangal, lemongrass, 1 tbsp shrimp paste, 1 tbsp turmeric, 2 tsp coriander) followed, compared with Wikipedia on the Shan and Northern origin and the blood cake. Dok ngiao and thua nao left out, as SBS does. Stock 8 servings of 1 cup assumed (about 2 litres).

recipes.name: Khao Pad (Thai Fried Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fluffy day-old jasmine rice fried hot with egg, shallot and garlic, lightly salty from fish sauce and thin soy, brightened at the table with lime and chili fish sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Egg and chicken make it a filling plate with protein, and the cucumber and herbs on the side add a little freshness to a mostly starchy dish.

components.note: cooked jasmine rice, a day old and cold

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over medium high heat and fry the shallot and garlic until fragrant, 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Add the chicken and fry until just cooked, 2 to 3 minutes, then push it aside, crack in the eggs and scramble them until nearly set, about 1 minute.
Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps, and toss over high heat until every grain is hot and coated, 2 to 3 minutes.
Season with the fish sauce and thin soy, add the tomato and toss for 1 minute more, then fold in the green onion, cilantro and white pepper.
Serve with sliced cucumber, a lime wedge and chili fish sauce on the side.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the fish sauce, thin soy and chili fish sauce.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Thai Fried Rice
Wikipedia, Khao phat

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai (serves 3: 3 tbsp shallot, 2 garlic, 3 cups cooked jasmine rice, 2 eggs, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp thin soy, 3 tbsp green onion, 3 tbsp cilantro, white pepper, lime) followed, with chicken and tomato added as Wikipedia describes the common Central version, served with cucumber, lime and phrik nam pla. Rice is 3 servings of 1 cup and nam pla prik 3 servings of 1 tbsp from the bases file.

recipes.name: Khao Man Gai (Chicken and Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky poached chicken over rice cooked in the chicken fat and broth, rich with garlic and ginger, cut by a sharp, salty soybean, ginger and chili sauce and a cup of clear broth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Poached chicken gives plenty of protein and the broth is gentle and warming, though the rice cooked in chicken fat makes this a fairly rich plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: 12 cups for poaching, 1 cup for the soup

ingredients.baseName: Grains, rice, white, long-grain, regular, dry
ingredients.cutPrep: jasmine rice, rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Bring the 12 cups of water to a boil with the salt and 4 of the cilantro roots, lower in the chicken and keep it at a bare simmer until cooked through, 30 to 45 minutes, then plunge it into cold water for a smooth skin.

Fry the 30 g of garlic in the oil over medium heat until golden, 2 to 3 minutes, add the rinsed rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, then cook it with 3 cups of the broth, the ginger slices and the last 2 cilantro roots until tender, 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir together the soybean paste, palm sugar, dark soy, thin soy, vinegar, chilies, grated ginger, chopped garlic and 2 tbsp of the broth until the sugar dissolves.
Simmer the daikon in 1 cup of water and 1 cup of the broth until tender, about 10 minutes, and finish it with cilantro.
Slice the chicken and serve it over the rice with cucumber, the sauce and a small bowl of the soup.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the rice cooked in broth.
From the soybean paste and soy sauces.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Thai Style Chicken and Rice (Khao Man Gai)
Wikipedia, Khao man kai

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai (serves 6: 3 lb chicken, 1 tbsp salt, cilantro roots, 12 cups water; 2 cups jasmine rice, 3 cups broth, ginger, 2 tbsp garlic fried in 1/4 cup oil; 1/4 cup soybean paste, 2 tbsp palm sugar, 3 tbsp dark soy, 2 tbsp thin soy, 2 tbsp vinegar, 4 chilies, 3 tbsp ginger, 1 tbsp garlic; a winter gourd or daikon soup) followed, compared with Wikipedia on the Hainanese origin, the tauchu, thick soy, ginger and vinegar sauce, and the clear daikon broth. The chicken poaching makes the broth, so no stock base is listed. The soybean paste is marked gluten because many Thai brands add wheat.

recipes.name: Khao Moo Daeng (Red Pork on Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, five-spiced red roast pork and crackling pork belly over rice, drowned in a glossy sesame and soy gravy, with a boiled egg, cucumber and a sharp chili vinegar.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork and eggs give a lot of protein along with B vitamins, though the sweet gravy, sausage and crisp pork belly make this a rich, salty treat.

ingredients.cutPrep: 6 cloves for the marinade, 2 for the gravy, pounded

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
ingredients.cutPrep: Thai thin soy sauce, for the marinade

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
ingredients.cutPrep: Thai thin soy sauce, for the gravy

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
ingredients.cutPrep: Thai thin soy sauce, for the chili vinegar

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Pound the 6 marinade garlic cloves with the cilantro roots and white pepper, mix with the thin soy, oyster sauce, five spice, palm sugar, sesame oil and colouring, coat the pork and marinate it for 24 to 48 hours in the fridge.
Roast the pork at 350°F (175°C) until cooked through, 30 to 40 minutes, basting once, then rest it for 10 minutes and slice it thin.

Simmer the soybean sauce, ground sesame, thin soy, dark soy, the 2 remaining garlic cloves, palm sugar and stock for 3 to 5 minutes, then stir in the cornstarch and cook until glossy and thick, 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir the chili vinegar ingredients together until the sugar dissolves, and fry the Chinese sausage briefly until it browns, 2 to 3 minutes.
Lay the red pork, crisp pork belly and sausage over the rice, ladle over the gravy and serve with egg, cucumber, green onion and the chili vinegar.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork loin, pork belly and eggs.
From the soy sauces, soybean sauce and sausage.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Khao Moo Daeng
Wikipedia, Khao mu daeng

recipes.name: Khao Kha Moo (Stewed Pork Leg on Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Pork leg braised for hours until the skin is meltingly soft, sweet and dark with star anise, cinnamon and soy, over rice with a braised egg, sour pickled greens and a bright chili vinegar.
recipes.healthBenefit: The long braise gives protein and gelatin from the skin and the greens add vitamins, though the fat and the soy braise make it a rich, salty dish.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Pound the cilantro roots, garlic and peppercorns to a rough paste, fry it in the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat until fragrant, about 1 minute, then brown the pork leg on all sides, about 5 minutes.

Add the mushrooms, star anise, cinnamon, palm sugar, five spice, thin soy, dark soy, salt and water, bring to a boil, then cover and keep at a gentle simmer until the skin is soft and the meat comes off the bone, 2.5 to 3 hours.
Add the peeled eggs for the last 30 minutes, turning them once so they colour evenly.
Stir the pounded chilies and salt into the vinegar for the dip.
Slice the pork, skin and all, and serve it over rice with half an egg, some braising liquid, the greens, the pickled mustard and the chili vinegar.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork leg and eggs.
From the soy braise and pickled greens.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Khao Kha Moo

Wikipedia, Khao kha mu

recipes.name: Khao Pad Sapparot (Pineapple Fried Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Golden, curry-scented fried rice with sweet, juicy pineapple, plump shrimp, toasted cashews and a scatter of raisins, savoury and sweet in every bite.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp and egg give protein, pineapple brings vitamin C and the cashews add some healthy fats and minerals to a starchy plate.

components.note: cooked jasmine rice, a day old and cold

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the cashews until golden, 2 to 3 minutes, then lift them out.
Add the rest of the oil over high heat, sear the shrimp until just pink, 1 to 2 minutes, and set them aside with the cashews.
Fry the onion, carrot and garlic until softened, 2 to 3 minutes, push them aside and scramble the eggs until nearly set, about 1 minute.

Add the rice and curry powder and toss until the rice is hot and evenly golden, 2 to 3 minutes, then add the pineapple, raisins, thin soy, fish sauce, sugar and white pepper and toss for 1 to 2 minutes more.
Return the shrimp and cashews, fold in the green onion and serve topped with cilantro and fried shallots.

citations.source: Grantourismo, Thai Pineapple Fried Rice
Tara's Multicultural Table, Khao Pad Sapparot

recipes.name: Khao Mok Gai (Thai Chicken Biryani)
recipes.flavorProfile: Yellow turmeric rice steamed with cardamom, cloves and cinnamon around tender yogurt-marinated chicken, warmly spiced rather than hot, eaten with a sweet and sour cucumber relish.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken thighs give protein and the yogurt and spices are gentle, and the cucumber relish adds freshness to a filling rice plate.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, rice, white, long-grain, regular, dry
ingredients.cutPrep: jasmine rice, rinsed until the water runs clear

instructions: Mix the yogurt with 1 tsp turmeric, the cumin, coriander, 1 tbsp curry powder, ginger, garlic, fish sauce and half the salt, coat the chicken and marinate it for at least 30 minutes, up to overnight.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and fry the onion until golden, 6 to 8 minutes, then add the cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaves and the rest of the curry powder for 30 seconds.
Brown the chicken in the spiced oil, 3 to 4 minutes a side, then stir in the rice with the rest of the turmeric and salt until every grain is yellow and coated, 1 to 2 minutes.

Pour in the stock, bring it to a boil, then cover tightly and cook over the lowest heat until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through, 20 to 25 minutes, and rest it covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice around the chicken and serve with fried shallots, cilantro, a lime wedge and the cucumber relish.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the chicken thighs and yogurt.
From the cucumber relish and lime.

citations.source: Grantourismo, Southern Thai Chicken and Rice (Khao Mok Gai)
Nomadette, Khao Mok Gai

recipes.curationNote: Thai Muslim dish of the South. Grantourismo (serves 2: coriander, ginger, turmeric, cumin, 2 tbsp curry powder, bay leaves, 4 thighs; a rice of 3 cups jasmine rice with turmeric, cinnamon, 6 cloves, 6 cardamom and bay; cucumber pickle and fried shallots) compared with Nomadette (300 g thighs in 1/4 cup yogurt with turmeric, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, garlic, ginger and fish sauce; rice cooked in broth and rested 10 minutes). recipes.name: Jok (Rice Porridge)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smooth, creamy rice porridge cooked down until the grains disappear, with tender little pork meatballs, a soft-set egg, sharp ginger, green onion and plenty of white pepper.
recipes.healthBenefit: A soft, easy breakfast to digest that gives protein from the pork and egg and plenty of fluid, though the fish sauce and soy make it salty.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, rice, white, long-grain, regular, dry
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Bring the rice and water to a boil in a large pot, then lower the heat and simmer, stirring every 15 minutes so it does not catch, until the grains break down into a smooth porridge, 1 to 3 hours.
Season the porridge with 1.5 tbsp each of fish sauce and thin soy, adding water if it gets thicker than heavy cream.
Pound the garlic, cilantro roots and white pepper, mix them into the pork with the rest of the fish sauce and soy, and drop small balls into the simmering porridge until cooked, 4 to 6 minutes.
Crack an egg into each bowl, ladle the boiling porridge over it and let it sit for 2 to 6 minutes until the egg is as set as you like.
Top with green onion, ginger and white pepper and serve hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the fish sauce and soy.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Rice Porridge (Jok)
Wikipedia, Congee

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai (serves 6: 1 cup broken jasmine rice, 10 cups water or broth, 1.5 tbsp fish sauce, 1.5 tbsp thin soy; meatballs of 1 cup ground pork, fish sauce, soy, 3 garlic, cilantro roots, white pepper; 6 eggs, green onion, ginger; simmered 1 to 3 hours) followed, compared with Wikipedia on Thai jok as a breakfast dish with a raw or part-cooked egg, minced pork, spring onion, ginger and pickles. Water rather than broth was chosen.

recipes.name: Khao Yum (Southern Rice Salad)
recipes.flavorProfile: Rice tossed at the table with heaps of finely sliced herbs, crisp beans, pomelo, toasted coconut and dried shrimp, all pulled together by a deep, salty and sweet fermented fish dressing and lime.
recipes.healthBenefit: A large share of raw herbs, beans and fruit brings fibre and vitamin C, and the coconut and dried shrimp add some fat, protein and minerals.

ingredients.name: nam budu (Southern Thai fermented fish sauce)

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Simmer the budu with the water, bruised lemongrass, torn lime leaves, galangal, sliced shallot and palm sugar until slightly thick and syrupy, 10 to 15 minutes, then strain it and let it cool.
Grill the shrimp until just cooked, 1 to 2 minutes a side, and chop them.
Arrange a mound of rice on each plate with small heaps of shrimp, dried shrimp powder, toasted coconut, pomelo, the sliced beans, sprouts, cucumber, sliced lemongrass and lime leaves around it.
Serve with the dressing, sliced chilies, chili flakes and lime wedges, and let each person pour, squeeze and toss everything together just before eating.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pomelo, lime and raw herbs.
From the beans, sprouts and coconut.
From the budu and dried shrimp.

citations.source: Bangkok Glutton, What's Cooking: Khao Yum
Michelin Guide, Anatomy of a Dish: Khao Yam

recipes.name: Gai Yang (Isan Grilled Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, salty chicken with crackling bronzed skin, deep with garlic, cilantro root and white pepper and a little sweet from honey, eaten by hand with sticky rice and a sour, chili-hot jaew.
recipes.healthBenefit: A good amount of protein from the whole chicken, with the skin adding fat, so pair it with som tam or raw vegetables for freshness.

ingredients.cutPrep: one whole chicken, about 5 lb, split down the back and flattened

instructions: Pound the garlic, cilantro roots, white pepper and salt to a coarse paste, 2 to 3 minutes, then stir in the fish sauce, turmeric and honey.
Rub the paste all over the flattened chicken and under the skin, and marinate it in the fridge for at least 2 hours, up to overnight.
Grill it skin side up over slow charcoal, or roast it at 350°F (175°C) for about 1 hour, turning it once and giving it 15 to 20 minutes on the second side.
Finish skin side up under the broiler or over hotter coals until the skin is crisp and spotted dark, 5 to 8 minutes.
Rest it for 10 minutes, chop it through the bone and serve it with sticky rice, jaew and cucumber.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the sticky rice on the side.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Thai Grilled Chicken
Wikipedia, Kai yang

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai (serves 6: 1 head garlic, 1 tsp salt, 1.5 tsp white pepper, 3 tbsp honey, a 5 lb chicken, at least 2 hours, 350°F for 1 hour then 20 minutes on the second side and 8 minutes under the broiler; som tam, sticky rice and nam jim jaew) followed, with the fish sauce, turmeric and coriander root that Wikipedia names for the Isan marinade and its slow charcoal grilling. Sticky rice is 4 servings of 1 cup and jaew 6 servings of 1 tbsp from the bases file.

recipes.name: Moo Ping (Grilled Pork Skewers)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin, tender pork on skewers, sweet and savoury with a caramelised edge from palm sugar and oyster sauce, milk-soft inside, eaten with sticky rice in the morning.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean pork gives protein, though the sweet marinade and soy sauces make it fairly high in sugar and salt, so this is best as part of a meal with vegetables.

ingredients.cutPrep: tenderloin, sliced thin and wide for skewering

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Pound the garlic, white pepper and cilantro roots to a paste, 2 to 3 minutes.
Mix the paste with the thin soy, oyster sauce, dark soy, both sugars and the milk until the sugar dissolves, add the pork and marinate it in the fridge for at least 2 hours, up to overnight.
Thread the pork onto soaked bamboo skewers, bunching it so each skewer is thick in the middle.
Grill over medium charcoal, brushing with oil and a little coconut milk, until browned and cooked through, about 5 minutes a side.
Serve hot with sticky rice and jaew.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the soy and oyster sauces.
From the sticky rice and palm sugar.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Thai Grilled Pork Skewers
Wikipedia, Mu ping

recipes.curationNote: Rachel Cooks Thai (serves 4: 680 g tenderloin, 10 garlic, 1.5 tsp white pepper, 2 cilantro roots, 2 tbsp thin soy, 2 tbsp oyster, 1/2 tbsp dark soy, 1 tsp sugar, 1.5 tbsp palm sugar, 1 cup milk, oil to brush and coconut milk to baste, about 5 minutes a side) followed, compared with Wikipedia on the coriander root, garlic and palm sugar marinade, the milk or soy base and sticky rice with jaew. The database has no raw tenderloin, so the raw loin row stands for it (tenderloin is a loin cut). Sticky rice 4 servings of 1 cup and jaew 4 servings of 1 tbsp from the bases file.

recipes.name: Satay Gai (Chicken Satay)
recipes.flavorProfile: Golden, turmeric-yellow chicken on skewers, fragrant with curry powder and coconut milk and lightly charred, dipped in a sweet, rich peanut sauce with a sharp cucumber relish beside it.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken breast is lean protein, and the peanut sauce and coconut milk add fat, so the cucumber relish brings welcome freshness to a rich plate.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Mix 120 ml of the coconut milk with the curry powder, turmeric, sugar, salt and thin soy, add the chicken and marinate it in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Thread the chicken onto soaked bamboo skewers.
Grill over low to medium charcoal, basting with the last 60 ml of coconut milk, until browned and cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes a side.
Serve hot with the peanut sauce and the cucumber relish.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the coconut milk and peanut sauce.
A little from the cucumber relish.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Easy Chicken Satay
Import Food, Chicken Satay (Satay Gai)

Rachel quantities kept with Import Food turmeric, soy and basting. Nam jim satay 8 servings of 1 tbsp and ajad 4 servings of 2 tbsp from the bases file.

recipes.name: Kor Moo Yang (Grilled Pork Neck)
recipes.flavorProfile: Juicy, well-marbled pork neck charred over coals, peppery and savoury from oyster sauce and soy, sliced thin and dipped in a smoky, sour, roasted-rice jaew.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork neck gives protein and B vitamins, and it is a fatty cut, so the cucumber and herbs alongside lighten the plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: pork neck (collar), from the shoulder, in 2 to 3 thick pieces

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Pound the garlic, coriander seed and cilantro roots to a paste, 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the oyster sauce, thin soy, dark soy, white pepper, palm sugar, milk and water, coat the pork and marinate it in the fridge for at least 30 minutes, up to overnight.
Grill over medium charcoal, turning now and then, until cooked through with a charred crust, 20 to 30 minutes, or roast at 437°F (225°C) for about 30 minutes, turning halfway.
Rest it for 5 minutes, slice it thin across the grain and serve with jaew, sticky rice, cucumber and cilantro.

nutritionHighlights.note: Pork is one of the richer sources of vitamin B1.

citations.source: Cooking with Nart, Thai Grilled Pork Neck (Kor Moo Yang)

recipes.curationNote: Cooking with Nart (1.5 lb pork neck, 1.5 tbsp oyster, 1.5 tbsp soy, 1/2 tbsp black soy, 1 tbsp white pepper, 1 tbsp water, 30 minutes, 437°F for 30 minutes turned halfway; jaew, sticky rice and vegetables) followed, with the garlic, coriander seed, coriander root, palm sugar and milk from Hungry in Thailand (serves 4: 1.5 lb pork, 4 hours, charcoal until charred). Pork neck is not in the database, so the raw shoulder row stands for the collar, which is cut from the shoulder. Sticky rice 4 servings of 1 cup and jaew 6 servings of 1 tbsp from the bases file.

recipes.name: Tod Mun Pla (Fish Cakes)
recipes.flavorProfile: Springy, bouncy little fish cakes, red with curry paste and flecked with makrut leaf and crunchy long bean, fried golden and dipped in a sweet, sour cucumber relish with peanuts.
recipes.healthBenefit: White fish gives lean protein, and frying adds fat, so these are a snack or starter to share rather than a whole meal.

ingredients.cutPrep: one whole egg and one white
about 60 ml taken up from 500 ml of frying oil

instructions: Pound or process the fish to a smooth, sticky paste, 3 to 5 minutes, then work in the curry paste.
Add the egg, tapioca starch, fish sauce, sugar and salt and keep pounding or stirring until the mixture is springy, then fold in the makrut leaves and long beans.
Chill the mixture for at least 30 minutes, up to overnight, so it firms up.
With wet hands, shape it into small flat patties about 5 cm across.
Shallow fry in batches over medium heat, turning once, until puffed and golden, 3 to 4 minutes a batch, and drain.
Serve hot with the cucumber relish scattered with crushed peanuts.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the white fish and egg.
From the frying oil and peanuts.
From the curry paste and fish sauce.

citations.source: Import Food, Spicy Thai Fish Cakes (Tod Man Pla)
Hungry in Thailand, Tod Mun Pla

recipes.curationNote: Import Food (serves 4: 450 g white fish, 1 egg plus 1 white, 3/4 cup long beans, 6 makrut leaves, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 1.5 tbsp red curry paste, fried over medium heat, ajad with peanuts) compared with Hungry in Thailand (1 lb fish, 2 tbsp curry paste, 5 makrut leaves, 2 tbsp tapioca starch, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 egg, 1/2 tbsp sugar, 2 long beans, chilled at least 1 hour). recipes.name: Seua Rong Hai (Crying Tiger Steak)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky charred beef, pink inside and sliced thin, dipped in a fiercely hot, sour and salty jaew with toasted rice, cooled by cucumber, long beans and sticky rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef brings protein, iron and zinc, and the raw vegetables alongside add crunch and a little fibre.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.cutPrep: cut in 8 cm lengths, raw, to serve

instructions: Rub the beef with the thin soy and marinate it for 1 hour.
Grill over hot charcoal to rare or medium rare, 4 to 6 minutes a side.
Rest it for 5 to 10 minutes, then slice it thin across the grain.
Serve with the jaew for dipping, raw cucumber and long beans, and sticky rice.

citations.source: Import Food, Crying Tiger Beef (Seua Rong Hai)
Wikipedia, Suea rong hai

recipes.curationNote: Import Food (serves 4: 1 lb flank in 2 tbsp thin soy for 1 hour, charcoal, a sauce of coriander seed, garlic, chilies, lime, fish sauce and sugar, with cucumber, green beans and sticky rice) compared with Wikipedia (Lao and Isan, grilled rare, nam chim chaeo with roasted rice). The jaew base with toasted rice stands for the sauce as Wikipedia describes it, so the Import Food sauce is not repeated. Jaew 8 servings of 1 tbsp and sticky rice 4 servings of 1 cup from the bases file.

recipes.name: Pla Rad Prik (Fried Fish with Chili Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: A whole fish fried shatteringly crisp, smothered in a glossy sweet, sour and hot sauce of garlic, red chilies, palm sugar and tamarind.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fish gives lean protein, while deep frying and the sugary sauce make this a richer dish to share with rice and vegetables.

ingredients.cutPrep: one whole fish, scaled and gutted, scored 3 to 4 times on each side

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.cutPrep: about 45 ml taken up from 500 ml of frying oil

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green
ingredients.cutPrep: red bird's eye chilies, roughly chopped

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Pat the scored fish dry and dust it lightly with the flour.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat to about 280 to 350°F (140 to 175°C), lower the fish in and fry it without moving until crisp and golden, 6 to 8 minutes a side.
Drain it on a rack; for an extra crisp skin bake it at 350°F (175°C) for about 10 minutes.
Pound the garlic and chilies coarsely, then fry them in 1 tbsp fresh oil over medium low heat until fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the tamarind water, palm sugar, fish sauce and water and simmer until sticky, 3 to 5 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the fish, scatter with green onion and serve with jasmine rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the palm sugar in the sauce.

citations.source: Import Food, Thai Crispy Fish Topped with Chili Sauce (Pla Rad Prik)
Thai Cookbook TV, Fried Fish with Sweet Chili and Garlic Sauce

recipes.curationNote: Import Food (serves 4: 1 lb tilapia, 2 tbsp garlic, 7 red chilies, 2 tbsp palm sugar, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp tamarind with 1 tbsp water, 1/4 cup water, fried about 8 minutes a side then 350°F for 10 minutes) compared with Thai Cookbook TV (1 large whole tilapia dusted in 2 tbsp flour, fried at 140°C, a sauce of garlic, chilies, 2 tbsp coconut sugar and 2 tbsp fish sauce cooked until sticky). Import Food sauce kept with the flour dusting from Thai Cookbook TV. Only the oil the fish takes up is counted. Nam makham 2 servings of 1 tbsp and rice 4 servings of 1 cup from the bases file.

recipes.name: Kai Jeow (Thai Omelette)
recipes.flavorProfile: A puffy, lacy omelette fried in hot oil until crisp and golden at the edges and soft in the middle, salty with fish sauce, over jasmine rice with a squirt of sriracha.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs give protein, choline and vitamin B12, and frying in oil makes it richer than a plain omelette.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 30 ml taken up from 250 ml of frying oil

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Beat 2 eggs with 1 tsp fish sauce in a jug with a spout until fully combined and a little frothy.
Heat about 1.5 cm of oil in a small wok to 375°F (190°C).
Pour the egg in from a little height so it puffs and bubbles, and fry until the underside is golden, about 30 seconds.
Flip it with a spider, fry the second side for a few seconds, then lift it out over a plate of rice.
Repeat with the other 2 eggs, then top with green onion, cilantro and sriracha.

citations.source: Wikipedia, Khai chiao
Grantourismo, Thai Omelette Recipe

Only the oil the omelettes take up is counted. Rice 2 servings of 1 cup from the bases file.

recipes.name: Pla Pao (Salt-Crusted Grilled Fish)
recipes.flavorProfile: Moist, steamy white fish scented with lemongrass and makrut from the inside, its salt crust peeled back at the table, wrapped in lettuce with noodles and herbs and dipped in a sour, hot seafood sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fish cooked in its skin gives lean protein with very little added fat, and the lettuce and herbs make it a light, fresh meal.

ingredients.cutPrep: one whole fish, about 2 lb, scaled and gutted

ingredients.name: lemongrass
ingredients.cutPrep: 2 stalks, bruised and cut to fit the belly

ingredients.name: coarse salt for the crust, peeled away with the skin and not eaten

instructions: Pat the fish dry and stuff the belly with the lemongrass and makrut leaves.
Pat the coarse salt all over the outside, about 0.5 cm thick, and rest the fish for 15 minutes so the crust sets.
Grill over low to medium charcoal, turning once, until the flesh flakes and reaches 145°F (63°C) at the thickest part, 25 to 30 minutes.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until tender, 3 to 4 minutes, and rinse them in cold water.
Peel back the salt crust and skin at the table and wrap the fish in lettuce with noodles and herbs, dipping each bite in the seafood sauce.

citations.source: Rachel Cooks Thai, Salt Crusted Grilled Fish
Hungry in Thailand, Pla Pao

recipes.name: Gai Tod Hat Yai (Hat Yai Fried Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Deeply garlicky, peppery wings with a thin, dark, crackling rice flour crust, piled with crisp fried shallots and eaten with sticky rice and sweet chili sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken gives protein, and deep frying with the skin on makes this a rich treat best shared with vegetables.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 10 wings, poked all over with a fork
about 90 ml taken up from 1500 ml of frying oil

instructions: Pound the garlic, coriander seed and cilantro roots to a smooth paste, 3 to 5 minutes, then pound in the white pepper.
Knead the paste, fish sauce and sugar into the wings by hand and marinate them in the fridge for at least 2 hours, up to overnight.
Toss the wings in the rice flour until evenly coated.
Fry a few at a time in oil over medium low heat until golden and cooked through, 12 to 15 minutes, then drain and cool slightly.
Raise the heat to high and fry them again until dark brown and crackling, 2 to 3 minutes, then drain on a rack.
Pile the fried shallots over the wings and serve with sticky rice and sweet chili sauce.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the skin and frying oil.
From the rice flour crust and sticky rice.

recipes.name: Goong Ob Woon Sen (Baked Shrimp with Glass Noodles)
recipes.flavorProfile: Slippery glass noodles soaked in a peppery, savoury sauce and smoky bacon fat, steamed in a covered pot under sweet shrimp, ginger and a handful of Chinese celery.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp gives lean protein and selenium, while the bacon fat and soy sauces make it salty, so a side of greens balances it.

ingredients.baseName: Glass noodles made from mung bean starch
ingredients.cutPrep: dry, soaked until soft and drained
shell on, back slit and deveined

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Stir together the water, oyster sauce, dark soy, seasoning sauce, sesame oil and sugar.
Soak the glass noodles in water until soft but still a little firm, 10 to 15 minutes, drain them and toss them in the sauce.
Lay the bacon in a clay pot or heavy lidded pan over medium low heat and cook until the fat runs, 2 to 3 minutes, then add the garlic, cilantro roots and black pepper and sizzle for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the noodles and their sauce, scatter the ginger over, lay the shrimp on top and finish with the Chinese celery and green onion.
Cover, raise the heat to medium high and cook until the shrimp are pink and the noodles have drunk up the sauce, 5 to 6 minutes, stirring once halfway.
Garnish with cilantro and serve in the pot.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the bacon, oyster sauce and soy sauces.

recipes.name: Moo Tod Kratiem (Garlic Fried Pork)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin slices of pork fried golden in garlicky oil, savoury and peppery, buried under crisp, sweet fried garlic and eaten over jasmine rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean pork gives protein and thiamin, while the frying oil makes it richer, so cucumber or greens on the side are a good match.

ingredients.cutPrep: lean, sliced 0.5 cm thick and pounded thin

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.cutPrep: about 45 ml taken up from 250 ml of frying oil

instructions: Pound the half head of garlic with the cilantro roots, ground coriander, black pepper and chili to a paste, 2 to 3 minutes.
Mix the paste into the pork with the cornstarch, fish sauce, thin soy, sugar and sesame oil and marinate it in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.
Heat just enough oil to fry the pork in a wok over medium low heat and fry it in batches, turning once, until golden on both sides and cooked through, 3 to 5 minutes a batch.
Lift out the pork, scoop out any dark bits of garlic, then fry the chopped garlic in the same oil until light golden, 1 to 2 minutes, and drain it at once.
Pile the fried garlic over the pork and serve with jasmine rice, cucumber and cilantro.

nutritionHighlights.note: Pork is one of the richer sources of vitamin B1.

recipes.name: Kai Look Keuy (Son-in-Law Eggs)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft-boiled eggs fried until blistered and golden, halved to show jammy yolks and drenched in a sticky sweet, sour and salty tamarind sauce with crisp shallots and fried chilies.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs give protein, choline and vitamin B12, and the palm sugar sauce and frying make it a rich dish to eat with rice.

ingredients.cutPrep: about 30 ml taken up from 240 ml of frying oil
dried red chilies, fried until crisp

instructions: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 6 to 8 minutes for jammy yolks, then cool them in cold water and peel them.
Heat the oil to 375°F (190°C) and fry the dried chilies for a few seconds until crisp, then lift them out.
Fry the eggs in the same oil, rolling them, until blistered and golden all over, 2 to 3 minutes, and drain.
Simmer the tamarind water, palm sugar, fish sauce and water over low to medium heat until thick and syrupy, 3 to 5 minutes.
Halve the eggs, pour the sauce over them and scatter with the fried shallots, fried chilies and cilantro.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the palm sugar in the sauce.
